body:
No criticism was supplied this cycle — the objection source is absent — so the work here is adjudication between the selected account and the rival, not repair of a flagged defect.

What the rival genuinely adds: the account's diagnosis (recurring friction from underspecified agreements under shifting schedules) carries an unargued assumption — that all three flatmates want a specification. The rival names that assumption and offers a competing one: the disputes may be about whether the flat is a unit with obligations or three private lives sharing fixtures, in which case a written standard is not neutral clarification but one side enacted. I accept that as live. The avoidance is at least as consistent with it as with ambiguity fatigue, both accounts concede the diagnostic uncertainty, and nothing in the material decides it. So the operative question is what to do while both readings are live.

Where I revise the rival: it treats "writing things down" as the account's remedy and truce-shaped arrangements (owned zones, rotations with default outcomes) as its own. But an owned zone is a specification; a rotation with a default outcome is one too — it even contains the fallback rule the account asked for. The real difference between the remedy families is not explicitness versus informality but how much ongoing mutual audit the arrangement demands. A shared standard with a fallback notice requires the flatmates to keep evaluating each other; a zone arrangement specifies once and then minimizes exposure. Once that dimension is visible, the two hypotheses stop forcing different remedies: low-exposure specifications work under both readings. Under the ambiguity reading they close the specification gap; under the unit-versus-privacy reading they remove the felt obligation to be audited. Given conceded uncertainty, the remedy that works on both readings goes first.

That also revises the rival's diagnostic test. Watching whether the avoider engages with a proposal's content or recoils from the idea of a written arrangement is weak evidence: rejection confounds disliking the content, disliking explicitness, and disliking the feeling of losing, and engagement can be sullen compliance. A cleaner version: present two concrete formats differing mainly in exposure — a shared standard with a fallback rule versus owned zones or defaults with no mutual audit — and let the preference between two real options carry the diagnostic weight. Nothing is delayed, since both options are actionable, and a preference between concrete arrangements is less confounded than a reaction to a proposal's existence. It remains weak evidence about what anyone thinks the flat "is" — people choose zones for convenience — but it is strong evidence about which remedy to install, which is the question that needs answering first.

Sequencing: I reject the rival's opening move as designed (separate conversations asking what the flat is). That question is abstract, high-stakes, close to the referendum shape the avoider is already declining, and it postpones relief on recurring items. Instead, keep the account's approach to contact — one-to-one, narrow, low-stakes — but change what is brought: not a drafted shared note as the only option (that picks a side prematurely), and not the ontology question, but the two formats. The abstract conversation becomes appropriate later, if a concrete failure gives it something to attach to.

The revised sequence: (1) One-to-one with each flatmate; no group summit, no moral vocabulary, no instance-counting — kept from the account, and reinforced by the rival's own symmetry objection, since "pulling your weight" rhetoric imposes the unit reading and scorekeeping is audit escalation. (2) For the two or three most recurring chores, offer both formats and ask which they would rather live under; state the limits plainly — bins and shared shopping resist zoning, and default-outcome arrangements sometimes mean the thing does not get done. (3) Install the chosen format as a time-limited draft, preserving the account's recurrence test. (4) After a few weeks, read the results jointly: recurrence falls — the friction was substantially specification-shaped, done for now under either reading; recurrence persists despite genuine engagement — the specification hypothesis weakens and the rival's axis becomes likelier; refusal to engage with either format, even the low-exposure one offered privately — the strongest available signal that the dispute is not about chore content. (5) Where account and rival converge, treat it as the most robust component: arriving independently, both end at the same escalation condition — if concrete low-pressure attempts fail, the question becomes whether the living arrangement fits, and it should be named rather than indefinitely deferred. I keep that unchanged, now with two grounds instead of one.

Left open: which reading is true, whether the avoider is acting in good faith, and whether the third flatmate contributes friction the material does not mention. None of that blocks the sequence, which is the point of choosing a remedy that does not require settling it.

One qualification on my own central move: zones are not perfectly neutral either. To a flatmate who holds the unit reading, being offered zones can feel like withdrawal of mutual care. The mitigation is offering the choice rather than installing zones unilaterally — which also happens to be the diagnostic.
